title: CFU Enumeration (Viable Plate Count)

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

purpose: To estimate the number of viable, culturable microorganisms in a sample by counting colonies that grow from a known volume of a known dilution.
principle: Each viable cell (or small clump, for methods that don't fully disperse clumps) that lands on the agar surface is assumed to grow into one visible colony; counting colonies on a plate within a countable range and back-calculating through the known dilution and volume plated gives an estimate of the original viable concentration.
requiredMaterials: Plates from the spread or pour plate method at multiple dilutions

procedure.instruction: After incubation, select plates that fall within the countable range specified by the method/reference you are following (commonly cited as 30–300 colonies for many general methods, but this is method-dependent — do not treat it as universal).
Count all colonies on the selected plate(s), marking each as counted to avoid double-counting.
Record the colony count, the volume plated, and the dilution factor for that plate.
Calculate CFU/mL (or CFU/g for solid samples) using the CFU Calculator.
If multiple countable-range plates are available across replicate dilutions, many methods specify averaging results — again, follow the specific method/reference in use.

observations: Distinct, separated colonies each counted as one CFU; overlapping/confluent growth is not countable and that dilution should be excluded.
interpretation: The resulting CFU/mL or CFU/g is an estimate of viable, culturable organisms under the specific growth conditions used — it does not capture viable-but-non-culturable cells or cells requiring different conditions to grow.
precautions: Confirm which countability range and averaging rule applies for the specific standard or protocol being followed before reporting a result.
limitations: Undercounts organisms that don't grow under the conditions provided.
Clumped or chained cells may be counted as a single colony, underestimating true cell number.
biosafetyNotes: Containment requirements depend on the organism being enumerated.
